reviews.body: This requires an additional change in our rig fork plus I don't think the current test is very robust.

review_comments.body: **Comment describes the wrong thing** The new `TimedOut` comment describes when execution selects this state: a timeout before `submit_result`. `CLAUDE.md` requires type comments to describe only the value, with conditions documented where the state is set. Move this condition to the timeout branch and describe the variant as a worker timeout with partial output. This repository requirement must be satisfied before merging. **Context Used:** CLAUDE.md ([source](https://github.com/mezmo/aura/blob/main/CLAUDE.md)) Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!

This reaches the agent but not the request. Rig's `create_request_body` copies `max_tokens` into `maxOutputTokens` only when `additional_params` already holds a `generationConfig`, so a plain Gemini config still sends no limit. See #861.

This checks the field set three lines into the Gemini arm, so it passes as long as that line exists, whether or not Gemini ever sees the limit. Asserting on the outgoing request body through a mock server would have caught #861.

Summary

The PR forwards configured `max_tokens` to Gemini and adds a regression test. The supplied changes also: - Tool results carry their kind so Aura can report real failures. - Gemini agents now receive the configured maximum token count. - Workspace packages move to version 0.2.20. One new type comment must be moved to satisfy the repository's comment rule. Acknowledged intent: `pcbeingused333` explicitly leaves Ollama forwarding out because its native API ignores the top-level field.
